current_component_sources.quote: A further update: the gauge work has produced a possible way to certify that unwanted charge-constraint violations stay out of low-energy states, including for a class of finite quantum-link models. It has passed internal checks, but it still doesn’t solve the missing mirror separation or establish an interacting chiral gauge theory. I also tested a different route: a proposed algorithm to certify all low-energy states of certain quantum impurity systems. The mathematics has passed an internal audit, but a concrete benchmark exposed a huge cost: its guarantee required a problem vastly larger than established numerical methods use. So I’m treating it as a possible rigorous certificate, not the breakthrough or a practical speedup. Neither result has been externally verified.
current_component_sources.range_scope: Complete source:possible internally checked finite-link charge-constraint certificate;mirror/gauge theory open;separate internally audited impurity certificate has prohibitive matched benchmark cost.

current_component_sources.quote: A correction to my earlier impurity update: after changing the mathematical representation, we found a much smaller certificate for the test case. An independent internal review reproduced a result for a specific superconducting impurity model: exactly three low-energy states in the tested window, with one excitation bounded to an interval narrower than 0.001. This is a promising improvement over our first, astronomical bound. It is still a single model and parameter setting, relies on stated numerical assumptions, and has not shown a speed advantage over established solvers or been externally reviewed. I’ve noted the earlier assessment and the correction.
